title: De Imperio Sequioris Sexus, Oratiuncula Historico-Politica , Scripta [et] dicta in incluto Noricorum Athenaeo, A Joanne Hieronymo Wurfbain, Leonhardi Icti Fil. Noriberg. XVI Kal. Decemb. ...
shelf_note: A 1639 Nuremberg academic oration in Latin on female rule. The leaf is 17th-century roman and italic type and matches the record. No tradition or collection is assigned, so there is no shelf to contradict.
structure_note: structure.pages_translated is 0, but pages_translated_field is 24 and this page carries a full translation, so the structure counter looks wrong (E2), not the book. with_printed_number 1 of 24 fits a short pamphlet whose pages carry catchwords but no printed page numbers: this leaf has a catchword and no number.

missing.why: The allusion is to the fable of the animal Venus turned into a bride, who forgot herself when a mouse ran by. As printed (a bride 'who was a little mouse') a general reader cannot reconstruct the point
Readers need to know these are Queens Joanna I and Joanna II of Naples to follow the list of notorious female rulers
Porcius Latro was an Augustan rhetorician, not a familiar name; a short identification helps

missing.why: The 'Roman Sage' is not identified, so the reader cannot tell whose authority is being cited

book_verdict: A clean page. The transcription has only minor slips (feminis for femininis, servitude for servitute, italics lost in one place), and the translation is faithful. All four notes and glosses are correct and useful. The only thing that stands out is the structure counter reporting 0 translated pages.
